core_obligations: Trivial direction (proof lines 20380-20383): if Q = 0 then all its cohomology groups vanish, which is immediate.

Bounded below case (proof lines 20385-20391): if Q is bounded below and nonzero, take the smallest i with H^i(Q) nonzero; the support lemma gives H^i(X, Q) = H^0(X, H^i(Q)) which is nonzero, so not all cohomology groups vanish.

General case (proof lines 20393-20400): let B be the quasi-compact objects of X_etale; the support lemma verifies the hypotheses of the sites-chapter statement, so H^q(U, Q) = H^0(U, H^q(Q)) for every U in B, in particular for U = X; since a complex vanishes if and only if all its cohomology sheaves do, the vanishing of all H^i(X, Q) forces Q = 0.
proof_roadmap: Handle the bounded below case by looking at the lowest degree in which the cohomology sheaf is nonzero.
For the general case, apply the sites-chapter triviality statement to the quasi-compact objects and specialise to U = X.
Conclude from the vanishing of the cohomology sheaves.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that for a complex on a scheme of finite type over a separably closed field whose stalks are supported at closed points, vanishing of Q is equivalent to the vanishing of all H^i(X, Q) (statement lines 20369-20377). The proof (proof lines 20379-20400) treats the bounded below case through the lowest nonvanishing cohomology sheaf and the general case by applying the triviality statement for cohomology over quasi-compact objects and specialising to X. H2: two short arguments from the support condition, written out.
